losses: a truncating open is not one transaction: `>` on an existing file is a truncate transaction followed by write transactions, so a crash between them leaves the truncated version
snapshot isolation is per open handle: reads use the pinned version, but `stat` on the inode reports the current version
the whole-file rewrite is bounded at 8 MiB (E2BIG above it); larger files need MW1 or a future range-write transaction
a write sequence is not atomic: each write is one transaction, and a refused later write does not roll back earlier ones
four concurrent same-inode O_TRUNC opens hit a pre-existing kernel-7.3 EIO under both MW1 and MW2 (measured in same_inode_trunc_control)
mode: optimistic (MW2 transactions); the default MW1 mount is exercised in H
role: T029 FUSE mutations under optimistic publication (MW2)

same_inode_trunc_control.interpretation: four concurrent O_TRUNC opens of one inode fail with EIO under BOTH modes on kernel 7.3; this is the pre-existing same-inode truncating-open limitation, not a T029 regression. Scenario C therefore uses a non-truncating whole-file write to exercise the transaction path.

scope.checked: six concurrent creates, four concurrent renames, four concurrent whole-file overwrites, four concurrent links and unlinks, an fd-spanning reader, eight refusals, offline verify --full, and the default MW1 mount
scope.label: one host, one local POSIX namespace, one mount daemon per mode; process-level concurrency
scope.not_checked: multi-node mounts, physical power loss, Go parity for FUSE mutations, byte-range writes that are not a whole-file rewrite, write-back/group-commit composition with MW2

semantics.create: one transaction: object record + directory entry, precondition Absent
semantics.link: one new directory entry in one transaction; directories refused
semantics.overwrite: read-modify-write of a whole file; the observed version is the precondition
semantics.read: an open handle reads the version it opened (snapshot isolation)
refused: a write past the 8 MiB whole-file rewrite bound (E2BIG)
semantics.rename: target entry (and replaced object when unreferenced) plus source entry in one transaction
semantics.unlink: entry removal plus object/relation removal when the last name goes, one transaction

c_concurrent_overwrite.method: four 8-byte writes at offset 0 with conv=notrunc; the last publisher wins and no splice of two writers is possible
